families.label: Price a job
families.card: An estimate with every quantity measured and sourced, and a page your customer can accept and pay.
families.description: Use when a tradesperson wants a job priced: an estimate, a quote, a bid or a takeoff from anything they have (a plan set of any size, phone photos, a customer's email, a voice note, the job in words, a home-inspection report). Covers reading and measuring, building sourced lines, marking assumptions, what to ask, and saving it as a card and a page their customer can open and pay.

families.label: Get paid on a job
families.say: Get a deposit on this job:
families.card: A deposit or invoice your customer pays by card, a pay application in the GC's format, or the dates that protect your payment.
families.description: Use when a tradesperson wants to get paid on a job: a deposit, an invoice, a progress bill, a pay application (AIA G702/G703 or a GC's own form, with retainage), a list of who owes what, or the deadlines that protect their payment (preliminary notices, notices of furnishing, lien dates, prompt-payment interest). Creates payment requests their customer pays by card on the owner's own Stripe, with AMTECH's 8% said plainly.

families.label: Get on property managers' vendor lists
families.say: Get me on property managers' approved-vendor lists. My trade and area:
families.card: The managers near you who hire your trade, what each requires, and your vendor file with what is missing.
families.description: Use when a tradesperson wants repeat work from property managers, HOA or community managers, or facility managers: getting on approved-vendor lists, a vendor packet, a credentialing portal (RealPage Vendor Credentialing, NetVendor and the like), a rejected vendor file, a certificate of insurance a manager keeps asking for, or a payment held for a missing document.

families.label: Get on general contractors' bid lists
families.say: Which general contractors near me should I be prequalified with, and what do they need? My trade and area:
families.card: The GCs active in your county in your kind of work, each one's prequalification route, and your capability statement.
families.description: Use when a subcontractor wants commercial work from general contractors: getting invited to bid, prequalification with a GC (TradeTapp, BuildingConnected, a GC's own portal or form), finding which GCs are active nearby, a capability statement, or following up on bids that never turned into work.

families.label: Repair work from realtors
families.say: Get me repeat repair work from real-estate agents. My trade and area:
families.card: The agents with the most recent listings near you, an offer they can use, and repair estimates from inspection reports.
families.description: Use when a tradesperson wants repeat repair work from real-estate agents (inspection repairs, pre-listing work, punch lists before closing), or brings a home-inspection report to price.

families.label: Answer the inquiries coming in
families.say: Answer this customer inquiry and get them booked:
families.card: A reply to each inquiry with the estimate or next step it needs, and the questions that would change the price.
families.description: Use when a tradesperson cannot keep up with the inquiries already coming in (website forms, emails, texts, voicemails, marketplace messages), or pastes one and asks for a reply that gets the job booked.

families.label: Township, school and state work
families.say: Can I get township or school-district work? My trade and area:
families.card: The small-purchase routes open to you, the registrations each needs, and what is missing.
families.description: Use when a tradesperson asks about township, county, school-district or state work: small purchases and quotes, COSTARS in Pennsylvania, bid thresholds, public bid boards, vendor registration, or SAM.gov.

families.label: Turn finished jobs into reviews
families.say: Turn this finished job into a review and a post:
families.card: A job story from your photos, a review request for that customer, and the fixes your Google listing needs.
families.description: Use when a tradesperson wants more reviews, to show their finished work, or a stronger Google Business Profile: a job story from photos, a review request to a happy customer, or listing fixes.

families.label: Hire someone
families.card: A job post in your words, screening questions, and where to post it locally.
families.description: Use when a tradesperson needs to hire: a helper, a crew lead, an office person or a subcontractor, including the job post, screening questions, where to post locally, and sorting the replies.

families.label: Just bought the business
families.say: I just bought this business, and the seller is leaving. Here is what I have:
families.card: The business's written rules from what you give me, and the list of things only the seller knows.
families.description: Use when someone has just bought a trades business (or is about to) and needs its rules, customers, suppliers and habits written down before the seller leaves.

families.label: Inspection deficiencies into quotes
families.say: Turn the deficiencies in this inspection report into quotes:
families.card: A repair quote per deficiency from your parts and labour book, and the authority's report on time.
families.description: Use when a fire, life-safety or other inspection trade (fire alarm, sprinkler, extinguisher, backflow, elevator, fire door) brings an inspection report: deficiencies become repair quotes and the authority's report is filed on time.

families.label: Anything else your office needs
families.card: A growth plan, a contract read, an email answered, a spreadsheet, research. Tell it the work.
families.description: Use for any other office work a business owner brings: a growth plan, marketing, an email or a contract to read, a spreadsheet, a supplier dispute, a website fix, a policy, research, a letter. Nothing a business owner reasonably asks for is outside the job.
